match.reason: The closest bank point, eco-low-stable-inflation, teaches the same 2 to 3 per cent RBA target but is written for Victorian Units 3 and 4 and adds underlying inflation, which goes beyond the Year 9 and 10 depth of this brief, so a new point fits better.

draft.title: The inflation target
card: Inflation is a rise in the general level of prices over time. The RBA's target is to keep inflation between 2 and 3 per cent a year, on average.
On average means over time, not every month. Inflation can sit above or below the range for a while, and the aim is to bring it back.
Low, steady inflation helps people and businesses plan. They can guess what wages, rent and supplies will cost next year.
The target is not zero. Very high inflation makes prices hard to predict, and savings buy less each year.
draft.remember: The RBA aims for 2 to 3 per cent inflation on average, so people can plan.

a.q: Why does the RBA aim for low, steady inflation rather than rapidly changing prices?
opts: People and businesses can plan with more confidence
Prices stay exactly the same from month to month
The government can spend without limits on services
Wages and rents are fixed by law for each year
a.why: When inflation is low and steady, people and businesses can guess future costs and plan ahead. The target does not freeze prices, because inflation is a rise in prices over time and the aim is 2 to 3 per cent.
a.clue: Think about guessing next year's costs.

b.q: Inflation in Australia is 3.4 per cent this year, above the RBA's target. Over several years it averages 2.6 per cent. What does this show?
opts: The RBA can meet the target on average despite a high year
The RBA has failed, as inflation must stay within the range
The target applies only to a single year of price rises
Inflation of 2.6 per cent is too low to count as steady
b.why: The target is an average over time, so one year above the range does not mean it has been missed. An average of 2.6 per cent is inside the 2 to 3 per cent range.
b.clue: Does the target apply to every single year?

a.best: People and businesses can plan with more confidence

b.best: The RBA can meet the target on average despite a high year

problems.detail: The last line says 'The target is not zero' but then gives only reasons why very high inflation is bad. It never explains why the target is above zero, so the first sentence does not connect to what follows and could confuse students.

proposal.title: The inflation target
card: Inflation is a rise in the general level of prices over time. The RBA's target is to keep inflation between 2 and 3 per cent a year, on average.

Low, steady inflation helps people and businesses plan. They can guess what wages, rent and supplies will cost next year.
